lawRefs: Ohio Rev. Code 5747.02(A)(3)(c) (2026 and thereafter: $332.00 plus 2.75% of excess over $26,050)
Ohio Rev. Code 5747.025 (personal exemptions; none at MAGI of $500,000 or more from 2026)
Am. Sub. H.B. 96, 136th General Assembly (FY2026-27 budget), incl. uncodified Section 757.120(A) suspending indexing for taxable years 2025 and 2026
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed from R.C. 5747.02 as amended by H.B. 96 (effective 9/30/2025) and the LSC final analysis of H.B. 96; sha256 is of the canonical body. As of retrieval the Department of Taxation annual-tax-rates page listed years only through 2025, so the statute is the source. Law for taxable years beginning in 2026 and thereafter (nonbusiness income): if Ohio AGI less business income and exemptions is $26,050 or less, no tax; if greater, tax = $332.00 + 2.75% of the amount over $26,050. The $332 lump sum (a cliff at $26,050) cannot be expressed as marginal brackets: the brackets here (0% to 26,050, then 2.75%) UNDERSTATE tax by $332 for every taxpayer above $26,050. Same schedule for all filing statuses (joint filers get a joint filing credit instead of wider brackets). kind is "graduated" because of the zero band; economically it is a single 2.75% rate above the exempt band. Personal exemption per taxpayer/spouse/dependent is tiered by MAGI: $2,400 if MAGI <= $40,000; $2,150 if $40,001-$80,000; $1,900 if above $80,000; no exemption (and no joint filing credit) if MAGI is $500,000 or more in 2026. Amounts are the 2024/2025 indexed values (per 2025 IT 1040 instructions), unchanged for 2026 because H.B. 96 suspended indexing for 2025 and 2026. The maximum ($2,400) is encoded. No standard deduction. Bracket threshold and exemptions are indexed by statute to the GDP deflator (R.C. 5747.02(A)(5), 5747.025(C)) but indexing has been suspended by successive budgets, most recently for 2025-2026. Social Security and railroad retirement benefits are fully deductible. No pension exclusion; instead small credits: a small retirement income credit, a $50 senior citizen credit (65+) and lump-sum credits - each only if MAGI less exemptions is under $100,000. Business income: first $250,000 ($125,000 MFS) deductible, remainder taxed at flat 3%. Not modelled: municipal income taxes (levied by most cities on earned income, commonly 1%-3%) and school district income taxes; joint filing credit; other credits.

flags.brackets: simplified: statute imposes $332 + 2.75% of excess over $26,050 once income exceeds $26,050 (zero below); the $332 base amount is not representable and is omitted, understating tax by $332 above the threshold
flags.indexed: statutory GDP-deflator indexing suspended for taxable years 2025 and 2026 (H.B. 96 Sec. 757.120)
